subject: Forensic snapshot handback and limited retention exception request
messages:
From: Elena Park <procurement@genesihealth.com>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: forensic snapshot handback + limited retention exception

Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our compliance team have a follow-up ask before we finalize the contract. GenesiHealth has a regulatory requirement to retain debug traces for a subset of requests (investigative traces) for 180 days for a narrow tenant scope while an on-going audit is open.

Specifically we need:
- A documented forensic-snapshot handback runbook describing how you will take, store, and return a snapshot for tenant-123;
- Evidence that snapshots are isolated (KMS-wrapped, access logs, chain-of-custody);
- A sample signed attestation we can countersign that limits retention to tenant-123, enumerates access controls, and defines deletion procedure after the audit;
- CAIQ / SIG pointers that map to this exception path (we may include in our SOC 2 binder).

We understand this is an exception to your standard TTL for traces; please let us know what evidence artifacts you can provide and an estimated delivery timeline. I attached a short requirements summary.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Procurement Manager | GenesiHealth
procurement@genesihealth.com

Quick answers:
- Deliverables: forensic snapshot runbook (PDF), evidence pack (access logs, KMS key usage, proof-of-delete workflow), and an attestation template for countersignature.
- Timeline: initial evidence pack + runbook in 48–72 business hours, then legal redlines to the attestation (if any) to follow.

Looping in Marissa (Evidentiary lead) and Karthik (Sales & Procurement) to coordinate security/legal approvals and to confirm commercial terms for the exception. Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm we can scope this to tenant-123 and whether we require a separate order/commit for the SLA/retention variant?

Best,
Hiro

Irene — forwarding GenesiHealth's request (below). Short version: customer requests a 180-day retention exception for investigative traces for tenant-123 only. They want CAIQ/SIG mapping and an attestation they can countersign.

Can security produce:
- A forensic-snapshot-handback runbook (steps, roles, retention TTL, deletion verification) we can deliver to the customer;
- Evidence artifacts: sample access-log export, KMS key usage log, proof-of-delete manifest for a previous sample deletion;
- A signed-attestation template (we'll have Legal review) that restricts scope to tenant-123 and includes an expiry condition (audit closed or date).

Notes / constraints: the snapshot must be stored in an isolated bucket with customer-limited access and a short, auditable chain-of-custody. This is not a global change to our default TTLs — it's a tenant-scoped exception if we can get appropriate approvals. Also include any operational impacts (cost uplift, retention billable items).

Subject: Re: Request: forensic snapshot handback + limited retention exception — evidence pack and next steps

Elena / team — thanks for your patience. We prepared an initial evidence pack and a proposed operational runbook for the tenant-scoped forensic snapshot handback. See attached and notes below.

Attachments included: forensic_snapshot_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook), evidence_pack_v1.zip (sample access logs, KMS usage export, proof_of_delete_manifest.csv), signed_attestation_template.docx (template for your legal to review).

Summary of what we can support now:
- Scope: a tenant-scoped exception limited to tenant-123 (GenesiHealth) for investigative debug traces only. We will: take an encrypted snapshot, store it in a customer-dedicated S3 path with KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/EXAMPLE (access restricted to an internal custody group), enable immutable object lock for the snapshot object during the retention window, and retain only the minimal metadata required for chain-of-custody.
- Retention window and deletion: 180 days from snapshot creation. After the retention window or upon audit closure we will run the proof-of-delete workflow and provide a signed proof-of-delete manifest.
- Evidence mapping: the runbook explicitly maps steps to CAIQ questions A6.2 / A11.1 and to SIG artifacts for access control and key management (see runbook appendix B).
- Controls: role-based access, dedicated bucket, encrypted-at-rest, restricted KMS key usage, and request-level logging forwarded to a locked audit stream for customer review.
- Commercials: there is a modest one-time operational fee for snapshot creation and a small incremental storage/retention charge for the 180-day window; Karthik — can you prepare the quote line and confirm procurement steps?

Next steps (action items):
1) Elena / GenesiHealth: review attached attestation template and return any redlines to procurement@genesihealth.com. If acceptable, countersign and return to info-security@redwood.com.
2) Karthik: prepare a PO/quote covering the one-time snapshot and 180-day storage.
3) Marissa / Irene: we will provision a demo snapshot into a locked folder and produce the sample proof-of-delete manifest for your review (deliverable by 2026-05-15 EOD).

Proof-of-evidence links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleEvidencePack (read-only)
HubSpot case: HS-76129

If you'd like, we can set a short call this week (30 min) to walk through the runbook and the attestation wording before countersignature.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
